title: Which Private Houses Are Exempt from a Building Permit? (2025 Law)
desc: Private houses exempt from a building permit under Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025: floor and area limits, planning zones, and repairs or renovations.
summary: Conditions for a private house to be exempt from a building permit under Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025, and points to note when building without a permit.
body: p
Many rural homeowners wonder whether they need a building permit. The answer is in Clause 2, Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025 (effective from 1 July 2026).
h2
1. When is a private house exempt from a permit?
p

Under Point g, Clause 2, Article 43, a permit is not required for Grade IV works and private houses of fewer than 7 floors with a total construction floor area under 500 m², that are also not located in any of the following areas:
ul
Functional zones and urban development areas identified in a city general plan;
Functional zones, rural residential areas and urban development areas in the general plan of an urban area of a province or city, or in the general plan of an economic zone or national tourist area;
Construction areas identified in a commune general plan;
Areas that already have an architectural management regulation.
p

In other words, only small houses in areas not covered by the planning above are exempt. A house in a residential area under a commune general plan, or in an urban area, still needs a permit even if it has only 1 or 2 floors.
h2
2. Do repairs and renovations need a permit?
p

Under Point h, Clause 2, Article 43, a permit is not required for repairs or renovations inside a building, or for repairing an exterior that does not face an urban street subject to architectural management requirements; provided the purpose and function of use are not changed, the load-bearing structure is not affected, and fire prevention and fighting and environmental requirements are met.
h2
3. What must still be complied with when exempt?
ul
The house must still match the land use purpose and the approved planning (if any).
Design and construction must comply with standards and technical regulations and ensure safety for neighboring works under Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.

To have ownership of the house recorded on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ), the owner prepares documents under Article 148 of the Land Law; where a permit is required, the building permit is the most important document.
p

If you are not sure which area your house falls into, ask the land and construction officer at the commune or ward People's Committee, or request planning information under Article 55 of the Law on Urban and Rural Planning before starting construction.
note
This article is only a summary for reference. For the full text, see Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025.
